title: Growth Engineer
definition: A software engineer embedded in a growth or marketing team who writes code — experiments, A/B-test infrastructure, lifecycle automation, analytics instrumentation — to increase acquisition, activation, retention, and revenue.
definition_source: Pragmatic Engineer, "What is Growth Engineering?" (Alexey Komissarouk interview), https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/what-is-growth-engineering, 2025-03-20

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)

salary.source: ZipRecruiter (page slug: Growth-Engineering — different taxonomy, same role family)
Glassdoor (n=38 self-reported salaries — small sample, treat as noisy)

trend.claim: Growth engineering "was barely known a decade ago, but today, most scaleups and many publicly traded tech companies have dedicated growth teams." Discipline traced to Facebook's 2007 growth team under Chamath Palihapitiya; a fully-loaded growth team costs ~$1M/yr and needs $5M+ ARR to justify.

Growth Engineer is listed as a specialization branch off general software engineering, alongside Product Growth Engineer, Growth Hacking Engineer, Analytics Growth Engineer, and Growth Operations Engineer as adjacent/senior paths.

notes: Salary sources disagree sharply: two different ZipRecruiter URL slugs for what looks like the same role return $101,752 vs $146,868 averages, and Glassdoor's $359,824 average (n=38) is 2.5-3.5x every other source — almost certainly a small-sample outlier skewed by senior/Big Tech equity-heavy comp, not a representative median. Report the $100K-$240K band; flag Glassdoor figure as an outlier, not the headline number.

title: Growth Operations Engineer
definition: A systems-minded operator who builds and maintains the tooling, automations, and data infrastructure that keep a company's go-to-market engine — sales, marketing, customer success — fast, accurate, and scalable.

postings.note: Page explicitly states: "We could not find any 'growth operations engineer' jobs in United States."

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)
Built In (via web search, not directly board-counted)
postings.note: Listing's own URL slug reads "growth-operations-specialist" though the on-page title reads "Growth Operations Engineer" — title/slug mismatch.

salary.source: Growth.Talent guide (role: Growth Operations Manager, closest tracked title)
ZipRecruiter (role: Growth Operations Manager, closest tracked title)

trend.claim: Career-path guides place "Head of Growth Ops" and "Head of RevOps" as the two most common promotion paths out of this role, with senior people who reach Director/VP within 5 years typically developing engineering depth beyond no-code tools.

notes: This is the thinnest title in the set: exact-phrase postings are effectively zero on the one board that reports exact-phrase counts (SimplyHired), meaning the title barely exists as a standalone job-board search term — most real openings use "Growth Operations Manager," "RevOps," or "Growth Engineer" instead. The two salary sources for the closest proxy title (Growth Operations Manager) disagree by nearly 2x ($63K vs $117.5K median) — a real disagreement, not a typo; likely reflects ZipRecruiter's broader/junior-skewed sample vs Growth.Talent's SaaS-specific sample. Treat all numbers here as directional, not precise.

title: GTM Engineer (Go-to-Market Engineer)
definition: A technical specialist who designs, builds, and maintains the systems that power a company's go-to-market motion — enrichment workflows, outbound sequences, lead routing, and the integrations that hold the GTM stack together — sitting at the intersection of sales, marketing, and product.

postings.count: 5 (page shows individual listings, no explicit total-count string)

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)

salary.notes: 25th pct $110K, 75th pct $295K, 90th pct $397K — very wide spread.
Median from job-posting text; top named-employer comp: Vercel $252K, OpenAI $250K, LILT AI $221.5K, Air $208.5K, Ramp $184K.

trend.claim: GTM engineering job postings jumped from over 1,400 in mid-2025 to more than 3,000 by January 2026; postings surged 205% year-over-year; GTM Engineering job growth is roughly 13x faster than the broader tech labor market.
trend.source: Aggregated hiring-trend coverage (SyncGTM/Stacker/Apollo synthesis of GTME Pulse + Bloomberry data)

trend.claim: 1,000 GTM Engineering job postings analyzed; average years of experience required 4.11; SQL and Python each appear in 38% of postings.

notes: Best-documented title in the set — multiple independent postings analyses (Bloomberry's 1,000-job study, GTME Pulse) converge on similar growth-rate claims, and the stack data is postings-derived, not vendor marketing. LinkedIn's "11,000+" is loose-match noise; treat SimplyHired's 146 as the more defensible floor for exact-title US postings.

title: RevOps Engineer / Revenue Operations Engineer
definition: A hybrid engineering/operations role that designs, builds, and automates the systems powering the go-to-market engine — owning CRM architecture and data models so Sales, Marketing, and Operations run on one reliable, trustworthy pipeline.

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)

postings.count: 174,000+ (ZipRecruiter's own aggregate figure for the broad RevOps job family, per third-party citation)
postings.note: Cited via Fullcast's 2026 RevOps hiring guide, not independently confirmed by direct fetch of the ZipRecruiter page.

salary.source: Agents for Hire, "Revenue Operations Engineer Salary in 2026"
salary.notes: Same source notes company-size premium: $100K median OTE at 0-50 employees vs $162K at 1,000+ employees (62% premium); AI-fluent RevOps pros earn up to $60K more than generalists (~$200K vs $140K).

trend.claim: RevOps job postings grew 127% year-over-year between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026, and RevOps headcount grew at 3.2x the rate of all other GTM roles combined in the 12 months ending March 2026.
trend.source: CRM Today ("RevOps Is Now the Fastest-Growing Role in B2B Tech")
trend.confidence_flag: medium — trade-publisher stat, not independently cross-checked against a primary jobs dataset

trend.claim: By the end of 2025, 75% of high-growth B2B organizations were projected to have a dedicated RevOps function in place.
trend.source: GTM 8020, "28 RevOps Statistics and Revenue Operations Trends"

employers: Factorial (RevOps Engineer, via General Catalyst job board)
Ve — "the intent company" (Revenue Operations & GTM Engineer, via RevPath)
notes: Exact-title "RevOps Engineer"/"Revenue Operations Engineer" postings are rare (1-3 on SimplyHired) — most real hiring happens under the broader "RevOps" or "Revenue Operations [Manager/Analyst]" umbrella, where ZipRecruiter's own count balloons to 174,000+. That gap between exact-title and umbrella-title counts is itself the finding. GTM-Engineer-vs-RevOps-Engineer boundary is explicitly contested in the source material (one glossary source frames GTM engineering as sitting *inside* the RevOps function; treat the two titles as overlapping, not cleanly distinct).

title: Marketing Automation Engineer
definition: An engineer who builds and maintains scalable, data-driven marketing automation programs — primarily inside enterprise CRM/marketing-cloud platforms — turning one-off campaigns into automated, repeatable workflows tied to CRM and analytics.
definition_source: Synthesis of Artisan Talent and Hire Digital job-description templates, https://artisantalent.com/job-descriptions/marketing-automation-manager-job-description/ and https://hiredigital.com/job-descriptions/marketing-automation, 2026

postings.note: Page states: "No job results. To see more jobs, try:"

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)

trend.claim: Marketing automation manager/engineer-adjacent postings saw roughly 10% year-over-year growth across 2025; marketing-automation skills specifically commanded a 36% salary premium, and 78% of marketing leaders said they pay more for candidates with AI skills.
trend.source: Robert Half, "2026 Marketing job market: In-demand roles and hiring trends"

notes: Zero exact-title results on Built In and only 6 on SimplyHired — this is a niche title relative to "Marketing Automation Manager" or "Specialist," which are far more commonly posted. The two salary sources agree reasonably well (within ~9%), which is unusual for this dataset and worth noting as a rare point of cross-source agreement.

title: Growth Marketing Manager
definition: A marketer who finds, tests, and scales the channels that acquire and retain customers more efficiently, typically owning work across the funnel from first click to conversion — connecting strategy, experimentation, analytics, and revenue goals.

postings.count: 9 individual listings visible, no explicit total-count string on page

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)

salary.notes: 90th percentile $125,000; no explicit median/average captured, only 25th/75th/90th percentiles.

trend.claim: In New York, NY specifically, Growth Marketing Manager salaries range $124,556-$181,886 — significantly above the national Robert Half range, illustrating a strong metro pay premium for this title.

Marketing manager job postings overall were up 14% year-over-year in 2026 even as AI adoption in marketing hit 91%, though total marketing job postings remain down 27% from pre-pandemic levels — a bifurcated market where senior/strategic roles hold steady while execution-focused roles decline.
trend.source: Aggregated marketing hiring-trend coverage (Kalungi/Robert Half synthesis)

notes: Best salary agreement in the dataset in terms of source count (4 independent sources), though the range across them is still wide (~$91K-$177K depending on percentile/source) — normal for a widely-posted title with huge company-size and geography variance. This is the highest-volume title in the set by exact-phrase SimplyHired count (239).

title: Data Engineer, Growth
definition: A data engineer embedded on or serving a growth team, building the pipelines, event tracking, and analytics infrastructure (funnels, experimentation data, lifecycle triggers) that growth and product teams query to make acquisition/retention decisions — distinct from a general-purpose platform data engineer.
definition_source: Synthesis; no single named-source definition found for this exact hybrid title. General data-engineer scope from Indeed's job-description template, https://www.indeed.com/hire/job-description/data-engineer, 2026, narrowed to "growth" context via the one confirmed live posting (Roblox, Senior Growth Data Engineer).

postings.note: The single result is a Senior Growth Data Engineer role at Roblox, San Mateo, CA.

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)

salary.source: ZipRecruiter (general Data Engineer, national — no growth-specific aggregator found)
Levels.fyi (Airbnb Data Engineer specifically — Big Tech comp, not representative of typical market)
salary.geo: United States (Airbnb, total comp incl. equity)
salary.notes: Included for contrast only — total comp at a top-tier public tech company, not a market median.

trend.claim: Data engineering roles grew roughly 23% year-over-year with an estimated 260,000 open US positions projected across 2025; average 2026 US data-engineer salary cited at $153,000 ($120,000-$197,000 range); the field is getting "more specialized," with real-time/streaming (Kafka) skills the fastest-growing compensation segment.

notes: This is effectively a whitespace title: almost no employer posts the literal string "Data Engineer, Growth" or "Growth Data Engineer" — the one confirmed live posting is at Roblox. Everything else here is the general Data Engineer market used as a proxy, which is an honest limitation, not a finding about growth-specific pay. Treat this title as an internal specialization inside larger data-engineering orgs rather than a standalone job-market category.

title: Director of SEO
definition: The executive who sets vision, budget, and KPIs for an organization's organic-search function, operating inside a structured marketing org with peer directors and a defined revenue target — distinct from an SEO Manager by scope and reporting line, not by daily tactics.
definition_source: SEOJobs.com, "SEO Director: Salary and Job Description," https://www.seojobs.com/careers/seo-director/, 2026

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)

postings.note: LinkedIn's own topic-page title read "74 Head Of Seo jobs in United States (1 new)" — much tighter and more credible than the generic guest-search "X,000+" figure for the same board.

salary.source: Salary aggregator synthesis (cited as of July 2025)
ZipRecruiter (posted-job range, not a payroll-data average)

trend.claim: SEO hiring is tilting toward leadership: 59% of SEO job listings analyzed were classified as senior leadership roles (Director/VP/Head/Chief/Lead/Executive), based on a Semrush analysis of job listings referenced in third-party coverage.
trend.source: ALM Corp / dev.to coverage of a Semrush job-listings analysis, "SEO Job Market 2026: What 3,900 Job Listings Reveal"

trend.claim: 20.3% of SEO job ads now mention AI search, GEO or AEO skills as of June 2026, up from 12.2% in December 2025 (527 to 1,010 postings/month); postings mentioning AI-search skills carry a median salary of $117,500 vs $97,500 for those that don't — a 20.5% premium, across 13,779 US postings with advertised salaries.
trend.source: SearchForHire, "The Future of Search: 5 Experts and 328,650 Job Postings" (328,650 marketing postings of 632,840 total collected July 2025-June 2026)

notes: Director of SEO is a genuinely rare exact-title (19 on SimplyHired, 0 on Built In) compared to the broader "SEO Manager"/"Head of SEO" family. The SearchForHire study (328,650 postings, dated methodology) is the strongest single trend source in this entire dataset — primary, dated, large-n, and directly on-topic.

title: Head of AEO/GEO (AI Search Lead)
definition: The executive who owns an organization's full search function — traditional SEO plus AI-answer-engine visibility (AEO/GEO) — setting the long-term roadmap, managing a team of specialists, owning budget, and reporting to senior marketing/executive leadership on how search visibility ties to pipeline and revenue.
definition_source: Synthesis from Sloane Staffing, "AEO/GEO Hiring in 2026," https://www.sloane-staffing.com/insights/aeo-geo-hiring-2026/, 2026-08-11

postings.query: "AEO" "GEO" (both terms present, not exact phrase, United States)
postings.note: This is a broad co-occurrence count, not an exact "Head of AEO" title match — titles returned range from "Director, SEO & AEO" to "Technical SEO Specialist," i.e. mostly IC/manager roles, not just leadership.

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)
geojobs.ai (curated AEO/GEO-specific board, count not independently verified this session)

salary.source: Kaleigh Moore, "AEO Job Openings in 2026" (Experian posting example, manager-level)
Sloane Staffing, "AEO/GEO Hiring in 2026" (senior-enterprise band, content marketing w/ AI focus)
Same two sources, specialist-level band for contrast (Odoo posting example)

trend.claim: 50+ unique AEO roles tracked across 50+ companies as of July 6, 2026, including Stripe, Amazon, Pfizer, LinkedIn, Victoria's Secret, eBay, Palo Alto Networks, HubSpot, and Anthropic — spanning finance, healthcare, retail, and enterprise tech, not just SaaS/marketing.

720 postings in the last 12 months carry AI-search/GEO/AEO discipline directly in the job title; 28% of those are leadership roles (Director/Head/VP/Principal/Lead) vs. 15% for standard SEO titles — companies are hiring leaders, not juniors, for this new discipline.

94% of surveyed CMOs/digital leaders plan to increase AEO investment in 2026; 97% said AEO already had a positive impact in 2025; enterprises allocated an average 12% of digital budget to AEO/GEO in 2025.
trend.source: Conductor survey of 250+ CMOs, cited via Sloane Staffing

employers: Victoria's Secret (Director, AI & Organic Search — AEO, GEO, SEO)
Capital One (Senior Digital Marketing Associate — AEO, GEO and AI Search Lead)
J.Jill (Senior Manager of SEO & Generative Engine Optimization)
Stripe, Amazon, Pfizer, LinkedIn, Palo Alto Networks, HubSpot, Anthropic (named among the 50+ companies tracked)
stack: traditional SEO stack (GSC, GA4) retained alongside AI-visibility tools
notes: "Title alone tells you almost nothing about scope" for this category (direct quote from Sloane Staffing) — identical titles carry vastly different responsibilities across technical, content, off-site, and measurement functions, and the title itself is unstandardized (AEO Lead, GEO Manager, AI Search Lead, Director AI & Organic Search all describe overlapping work). This instability is itself the headline finding for this title. geojobs.ai is a purpose-built board for this niche but its live count wasn't successfully captured this session — flagged in notes.md as a gap worth a follow-up pass.

title: Growth Strategist
definition: A cross-functional role responsible for identifying and executing strategies — market analysis, competitive benchmarking, revenue-growth frameworks — that drive sustainable business expansion, sitting at the intersection of marketing, product, and data analytics.

postings.note: Single listing: BlackBox Strategies, senior-level, Professional Services/Consulting.

postings.board: LinkedIn (guest search, loose keyword match — NOT exact-title)

trend.claim: No title-specific "Growth Strategist" trend/surge article was found in this session (see notes.md gap). Best available context: 2026 hiring-outlook coverage names "digital marketing strategists, content strategists, and demand generation managers" as strong-demand roles for 2026, in a labor market otherwise described as "cooling."

notes: The 108 SimplyHired exact-phrase postings is a real, healthy-sized floor — but Built In returns just 1, and no dedicated 2025-2026 trend article specific to this title turned up despite several search attempts. This title reads as an established, steady-demand generalist role rather than an emerging/surging one — the opposite pattern from GTM Engineer or AEO/GEO leads.
